construct: Discrimination measures how well a model separates individuals who do and do not experience an outcome and is commonly summarized by the C statistic/AUC. Calibration measures agreement between predicted probabilities and observed outcome frequencies. A model can preserve discrimination yet be systematically miscalibrated in a new population.
